summary.title: How to code the "Game of Life" with React in under an hour
summary.one_liner: You learn to build Conway's Game of Life in React step by step: a CSS-gradient grid, clickable cells, a timed run loop, and the four survival rules.
keywords: convert click coordinates to grid cell
how to make a simple react game
canvas vs div rendering in react
takeaways: Draw a grid cheaply with CSS linear-gradient background instead of canvas.
Store board state in a 2D array and regenerate a list of cell components from it on each update.
Convert client-relative mouse click coordinates into board-relative grid cell indices.
Run a repeating iteration loop with window.setTimeout and stop it with clearTimeout.
Implement Conway's four rules by counting live neighbors for each cell per generation.
summary.summary: The author builds Conway's Game of Life using create-react-app and a single class component. The board is a div with a CSS gradient grid, cells are absolutely positioned divs generated from a 2D boolean array, and clicks are mapped to grid coordinates via getBoundingClientRect. A Run/Stop control uses window.setTimeout to advance generations at a configurable interval, and the next-state logic applies the four standard rules through a neighbor-count helper. The post is a short hands-on tutorial; the full source is linked on GitHub and the neighbor function is omitted from the article text.
